title: Integration of Network Toxicology and Transcriptomic Data: Exploring Molecular Associations Between Polystyrene Microplastics Exposure and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis.
authors: Zhang, Linbing; Wu, Jiarui; Ren, Yuerong; Wang, Xinya; Gao, Qingyao; Sun, Suju
one_liner_zh: 该文整合转录组与网络毒理学，通过分子对接初步探索聚苯乙烯微塑料与MASH相关转录因子（如JUN/AP-1）的潜在结合，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但非核心体系，方法以对接为主且深度有限。
abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs), persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutants detected in human tissues, have been increasingly associated with hepatic oxidative stress and inflammatory disturbances; however, their potential molecular relevance in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remains vague. In this study, we applied a systems-level integrative framework combining transcriptomic analysis, network toxicology, immune profiling, and molecular docking to explore the overlap between genes with curated chemical-gene interactions involving polystyrene in the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) and differentially expressed genes in human MASH liver tissues. By intersecting MASH-associated differentially expressed genes from the Gene Expression Omnibus with polystyrene-related genes curated in the CTD, we identified 80 candidate genes representing an overlap between curated polystyrene-gene interaction records and disease-related transcriptional alterations. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses further prioritized eight hub genes (MYC, ATF3, CXCL2, IL18, NOS2, SOD2, FASN, and ARG1) that were consistently associated with inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress regulation, and metabolic dysregulation. Immune infiltration analysis indicated close association of the hub genes expression with characteristic immune remodeling patterns in MASH. Upstream regulatory analysis identified several transcription factors (TFs) potentially involved in coordinating hub gene expression, among which JUN/AP-1 emerged as a central regulatory node linking inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolism-related programs. Molecular docking analysis provided structural support for the potential physical feasibility of interactions between a polystyrene pentamer and the selected TFs. Collectively, these findings establish a systems-level framework integrating CTD-curated polystyrene-gene interaction information with key transcriptional and immunometabolic features of MASH, generating testable hypotheses about the potential molecular relevance of PS-MPs to MASH for future mechanistic studies and environmental health risk assessment.
abstract_zh: 聚苯乙烯微塑料（PS-MPs）是一种在人体组织中检测到的持久性、生物累积性环境污染物，日益与肝脏氧化应激和炎症紊乱相关联；然而，其在代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）中的潜在分子相关性仍不明确。在本研究中，我们应用了一个系统级整合框架，结合转录组分析、网络毒理学、免疫谱分析和分子对接，以探索比较毒理基因组学数据库（CTD）中涉及聚苯乙烯的经整理的化学-基因相互作用基因与人类MASH肝组织中差异表达基因之间的重叠。通过将基因表达综合库（Gene Expression Omnibus）中MASH相关的差异表达基因与CTD中整理的聚苯乙烯相关基因相交集，我们识别出80个候选基因，代表经整理的聚苯乙烯-基因相互作用记录与疾病相关转录变化之间的重叠。功能富集和蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析进一步优先确定了八个枢纽基因（MYC、ATF3、CXCL2、IL18、NOS2、SOD2、FASN和ARG1），这些基因与炎症信号传导、氧化应激调节和代谢失调持续相关。免疫浸润分析表明，枢纽基因表达与MASH中特征性免疫重塑模式密切相关。上游调控分析识别出多个可能参与协调枢纽基因表达的转录因子（TFs），其中JUN/AP-1作为连接炎症、氧化应激和代谢相关程序的核心调控节点出现。分子对接分析为聚苯乙烯五聚体与所选转录因子之间相互作用的潜在物理可行性提供了结构支持。总体而言，这些发现建立了一个系统级框架，整合了CTD整理的聚苯乙烯-基因相互作用信息与MASH的关键转录和免疫代谢特征，为未来机制研究和环境健康风险评估提供了关于PS-MPs对MASH潜在分子相关性的可测试假设。
